text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000159's excess 99215 billing falls mostly on low-complexity patients, and most documented 99215 claims do not support the billed level, a pattern consistent with upcoding.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The excess 99215 volume sits mostly on patients with zero or one chronic condition. The sampled 99215 claims carry routine diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection (J06.9), rash (R21), low back pain (M54.50) and UTI (N39.0), which is not what a sicker panel would look like. The records review points the same way: the documented-below-billed rate on 99215 claims is roughly double the comparison rate. Examples such as C0066277 and C0066383 show only moderate MDM. Unsupported rates at 99214 and 99213 are also elevated, which suggests a general shift in coding level. The case is not fully one-sided. Some low-complexity 99215s did document high MDM, for example C0066270 (52 min) and C0066311 (46 min). The high duplicate-note rate and the notes claiming data review with no lab or test line on the claim raise a concern that some supporting notes may be cloned or inflated. That concern is weak evidence, not proof. A reviewer should first pull the full notes for the 15 unsupported 99215 claims and the four 'supported' ones. They should check whether the duplicated note text and the time entries reflect real encounter content, and then widen the records request beyond the roughly 19% of claims sampled so far."}
